title: Explain a Reported Conversation

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料；尚待独立教学与发音审核。

instructions: Prepare briefly and record your own response of 120–160 words. The sample is shorter than the 90–120 second target. Add relevant details and allow natural pauses while staying within 120–160 words.
prompt: Speak for about 90–120 seconds, using 120–160 words. Describe a fictional conversation with a reporter or event representative. Report one statement and one question, and explain a detail that still needs checking. Use at least six lesson words.
reference: I would speak with a representative of a local exhibition before writing a short report. She said that the event was planned for Sunday, and she told the journalist that a historical map would be near the entrance. I asked whether the map was an original, and she explained that it was a copy. A historian gave an explanation of the map, while a visitor shared a personal viewpoint about the building. The editor should check the transcript before choosing a sentence to quote. A volunteer might accept an offer to appear in a photograph, but she has not made that decision yet. I would ask for confirmation and inform the photographer that the answer is still uncertain. Our newspaper could describe these different perspectives without claiming that every resident agrees. I would make the limits clear to the reader.
